subject: Best practices: safer + cheaper blob browsing for agents (meta-first, multi-read, hardening against ambiguous filenames)

items.title: Prefer meta listing before reading content
items.rationale: Agents should avoid reading whole files just to discover names/sizes; meta reduces tokens and latency.
items.evidence: list_blobs include_meta returns name/size/last_modified so the agent can pick the right files first.
items.action: When exploring storage, call list_blobs with include_meta=1 and filter by prefix before any read.

items.title: Provide a single multi-read tool to reduce tool-call overhead
items.rationale: Reading many files one-by-one increases tool loop steps and cost; batching reads reduces round trips and model/tool chatter.
items.evidence: read_many_blobs reads multiple blobs in one call with explicit limits and optional tail extraction.
items.action: Use read_many_blobs for N>1 files and treat read_blob_file as a special case (N=1) or when content must be exact.

items.title: Harden read paths against ambiguous agent file references
items.rationale: Agents often shorten paths (e.g., 'index.jsonl'); a safe resolve prevents false negatives while avoiding wrong reads.
items.evidence: read_blob_file attempts unique suffix resolve only when basename-only and the match is unambiguous; otherwise returns candidates.
items.action: Keep basename resolve conservative: only auto-resolve when exactly one candidate exists; otherwise prompt the agent/user to choose.

items.title: Register tools in-process to avoid proxy fallbacks
items.rationale: Fallback proxies add latency and can break user_id propagation; deterministic tool dispatch should prefer in-process handlers.
items.evidence: read_many_blobs is registered in the tool registry and no longer routes through proxy_router.
items.action: When adding a new tool, update the tool registry and add a minimal integration test/run to confirm it is called in-process.
